summary: The note describes how local small businesses are coping with supply chain disruptions and inventory management problems that began around September 2023. Owners describe delayed shipments, rising costs and cash flow strain from over- and understocking. They have responded with local sourcing, technology, supplier diversification, a just-in-case inventory approach, staff cross-training and community collaboration.
one_line: Local small business owners respond to post-pandemic supply chain and inventory disruptions with local sourcing, technology, diversification, buffer stock, cross-training and collaboration.
key_facts: Supply chain disruptions for local small businesses were marked by early post-pandemic days around September 2023, when global logistics were on a delicate balance.
Jonathan McDougal, owner of McDougal's Electronics, described delayed shipments, skyrocketing costs, overseas factory shutdowns and shipping containers 'scarce as gold dust'.
Emily Watson, founder of Watson's Homewares, said inventory turnover was precise before the crisis, but October 2023 brought overstocking and understocking that severely disrupted her cash flow.
Alejandro Garcia of Garcia's Gourmet Groceries turned to local farmers and producers when imports became unreliable, gaining a steadier product stream and customer appreciation for local goods.
Bethany Ray, proprietor of Ray's Fashion Boutique, has used inventory and demand-forecasting technology since November 2023, calling it 'a game-changer'.
Marcus Li of Li's Hardware shifted to multiple suppliers after multiple shipment delays, saying 'It's about not putting all your eggs in one basket'.
Some small businesses have moved from a 'just-in-time' to a 'just-in-case' inventory model, building buffer stock, which ties up more capital but acts as insurance.
Sarah Chen, owner of Chen's Craft Corner, has used a just-in-case model since December 2023 and says it gives her peace of mind.
Kevin Roberts of Roberts Renewable Resources said cross-training employees let his business keep operating seamlessly despite external disruptions.
Melissa Grant, director of the Small Business Association, led an event on February 5, 2024 where small business owners networked and formed a coalition.
Community forums and alliances let businesses share insights, combine orders for better negotiating power with suppliers, and swap inventory.
